01 / From source to sentence

Keep the claim and the evidence together.

You have a recommendation to make and a room to convince. Bring your draft and its sources. The review brings an exact claim, its supporting passage, and a proposed edit into one place.

The difference comes after the edit: change the claim or its linked evidence, and the check needs another look. That is the workflow we are building, so yesterday’s review does not quietly stand in for today’s wording.

Connect Link a claim to a precise passage in your source.

Inspect See what the source supports and what remains uncertain.

Revise Preview and accept a scoped change, with undo.

Recheck Revisit changed claims before sharing your draft.

02 / Fewer hidden leaps

Better writing asks better questions.

A polished sentence can still hide a weak inference. The review is designed to bring four consequential questions into your writing process.

Does the evidence say that?

An interview is not the whole market. A correlation is not a cause. Compare the wording with the source and inspect a more precise claim.

A claim proportionate to its support.

What changed since the review?

A small rewrite can make a much bigger promise. When checked wording or linked evidence changes, revisit the claim before sharing it.

Visible review status for the current wording.

Can I inspect the reasoning?

Keep the source passage beside the finding. See what was supplied, what was inferred, and whether you agree with the proposed change.

A review you can examine.

What would change my mind?

Examine the strongest alternative, a pivotal uncertainty, or the evidence that would reverse your recommendation.

A decision that can be reconsidered.

A writing culture that grows with you

Make thoughtful writing a shared habit.

Good writing culture starts with better questions: What supports this? What else could explain it? What would make us reconsider?

Start with one memo. The longer-term vision is to carry that care across a team’s decisions, with the reasoning behind a choice still visible later.

The aim is a useful writing practice, with room for uncertainty and a change of mind.

A shared review standardPlanned
What are we proposing?A clear decision
Why this option?Evidence and alternatives
What remains uncertain?Explicit assumptions
When do we reconsider?Review conditions

Shared standards, team records, and organization-wide governance are roadmap capabilities.

03 / For the memo that matters

Before you ask for a decision, examine the case.

For product managers and founders writing a roadmap recommendation, launch memo, or investment proposal. Start with the document already on your desk.

01

Roadmap priorities

“Customers are asking for this.”

Which customers, in which segment, and how often? Keep a few interviews from becoming a claim about the whole market.

Bring customer evidence and the trade-off you are proposing.
02

Launch decisions

“The pilot proves we are ready.”

What did the pilot actually test? Keep its limits visible when the draft moves from results to a rollout recommendation.

Bring pilot findings and the conditions for expanding.
03

Investment proposals

“This will pay for itself.”

Which figures are observed and which are assumptions? Revisit the claim when a cost estimate or forecast changes.

Bring the business case and its supporting estimates.

An open foundation

Trust deserves a closer look.

The open-source engine makes our approach inspectable: frame the decision, examine evidence and reasoning, consider alternatives, and make the judgment explicit.

The five methods above inform the approach. They do not establish that an AI review is correct. You keep the source in view and the final judgment in your hands.

Explore the open-source engine
Can I start using it today?

You can try the interactive concept on this page, inspect the open-source engine, and discuss a design-partner pilot. The hosted writing app is not open for public signup or paid subscriptions yet.

What does a pilot cost?

We agree the scope and price before work begins. Start by sharing your memo type and review deadline. Public subscriptions and checkout are not open yet.

Will 🪔 diyalamp write the decision for me?

The aim is to help you develop and test your reasoning. Proposed edits should be visible, reversible, and accepted by you. The final decision stays yours.

Why use this alongside ChatGPT?

ChatGPT can critique a draft. 🪔 diyalamp is being built to keep each check attached to the wording and source it examined. When either changes, you can see what needs another look. The pilot tests whether this saves repeated review work.

Does a reviewed claim mean the decision is right?

No. A source can be incomplete or wrong, and AI can misread it. Review status concerns the supplied passage and the wording checked. It is not independent verification, approval from leadership, or a guarantee of business results.

Is this for essays too?

The approach is relevant wherever writing depends on evidence. Our first pilot focuses on decision memos for product managers and founders, where a weak claim can change what gets built, launched, or funded.

Does Defensive Writing mean defending my position?

No. A strong review can change the recommendation. The goal is a decision proportionate to the evidence, including honest uncertainty and the strongest alternative.
